title: CASMI26 COCONUT Morgan+MACCS Fingerprints
subtitle: 436k mass-sorted natural products with Morgan 2048 + MACCS bits, no pickle
description:
# COCONUT natural products with Morgan + MACCS fingerprints (CASMI26)

436,389 natural-product structures from COCONUT 2.0, **sorted by neutral monoisotopic mass**, with ready-made fingerprints for candidate retrieval in [Enveda CASMI 2026](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/enveda-CASMI26-molecule-id-mass-spectra). Plain Parquet + NumPy: **no pickle to load**, no RDKit needed to use the fingerprints.

## Files

| File | Shape / type | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| `coconut_structures.parquet` | 436,389 rows | `ik14` (InChIKey first block, the metric's identity), `smiles`, `mass` (neutral monoisotopic, ascending) |
| `coconut_fp_morgan2048_maccs167.npy` | (436389, 277) uint8 | Packed bits, row-aligned with the parquet: **Morgan radius 2, 2,048 bits**, then **MACCS 167 keys** (+1 padding bit) |
| `fingerprints.py`, `casmi.py` | code | `fp_packed_v2(smiles)` makes the same 277-byte fingerprint for any SMILES (e.g. the training structures); `formula_mass` for neutral masses |

All 436,389 SMILES parse; none has an empty fingerprint.

## Quick start

```python
import numpy as np, pandas as pd
D = '/kaggle/input/casmi26-coconut-morgan-maccs-fingerprints'
coco = pd.read_parquet(f'{D}/coconut_structures.parquet')
fps = np.load(f'{D}/coconut_fp_morgan2048_maccs167.npy', mmap_mode='r')

m = 348.1209                                   # neutral mass of the unknown
lo, hi = np.searchsorted(coco.mass.values, [m * (1 - 1e-5), m * (1 + 1e-5)])   # 10 ppm window
bits = np.unpackbits(fps[lo:hi], axis=1)       # (n_candidates, 2216): [:, :2048] Morgan, [:, 2048:2215] MACCS
cands = coco.iloc[lo:hi]
```

## Adding the training structures (about 2 minutes on 4 CPUs)

The competition's training SMILES can't be redistributed, so compute them in your notebook with the same function:

```python
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, D)
from multiprocessing import Pool
from fingerprints import fp_packed_v2
from casmi import formula_mass
tr = pd.read_parquet('/kaggle/input/enveda-CASMI26-molecule-id-mass-spectra/train.parquet',
                     columns=['inchikey14', 'normalized_smiles', 'molecular_formula']).drop_duplicates('inchikey14')
with Pool(4) as p:
    tr_fps = np.stack(p.map(fp_packed_v2, tr.normalized_smiles, chunksize=2000))
tr_mass = tr.molecular_formula.map(formula_mass).values
```

(RDKit is needed for this step: install it offline from [metric/rdkit-2026-3-3-wheel](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/metric/rdkit-2026-3-3-wheel).) COCONUT and the training set share no InChIKey14 here, so the two parts can simply be concatenated and re-sorted by mass.

## Matching models

These are the exact fingerprints predicted by the v2 model in [casmi26-spectrum-to-fingerprint-mlp](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/aryanawasthiteykik/casmi26-spectrum-to-fingerprint-mlp) (2,216 outputs), so its log-likelihood ranking works on them directly.
